description: issue #688 (terminal slice): the OTHER `ol-type` branch of `wait`'s tick count (spec/interaction-events.md:318 includes `ol-type` among `wait`'s errors; the profile error table at :435-439 gives `ol-type` for `an argument has the wrong type`). The sibling `wait-non-whole` covers a number that is not whole (`1.5`) and `wait-non-whole-word` covers a WORD that reads as a non-whole number (`"1.5"`); this one covers a value that is not a number at all -- the word `"soon"` -- so `params.actual` is `word` rather than `number`. Note this is NOT a blanket rejection of words: `spec/execution-model.md:33-34` makes "words that parse as numbers are accepted where a number is expected" a normative CORE rule, so `wait "2"` is legal and pauses for 2 ticks (pinned by the sibling `wait-numeric-word-accepted`). What this fixture pins is the complement -- a word that does NOT parse as a number is rejected outright rather than coerced to 0 or silently ignored, which for a pause primitive would be an invisible wrong result rather than an error. The `primitive` event is NOT emitted -- the pause never runs -- so only the instruction event precedes the diagnostic, matching every other failed `wait` validation, and the span covers just the argument. UPDATED by issue #775: `params.expected` now reads `whole number`, matching the `every` twin (`every/every-non-number-type-error`) for the identical non-number case. `spec/interaction-events.md`'s `### wait <n>` requires "a non-negative whole number", so the whole-number expectation is the right one for a value that is not a number at all -- and it is the spelling `every`, `repeat` (`spec/commands.md`'s `repeat` entry: "raises `ol-type` (a whole number is required)") and `random` already emit, all four now routing through the runtime's one shared `requireWholeNumber` check.
